findings.fix: Add a second independent mechanism, such as a breadcrumb trail (for example Home followed by Rider service updates) placed before #main-h1, or a site search form in #header, so a reader who lands directly on this page has more than one way to find it.
findings.location: #nav, <nav> element, the page's only navigation mechanism
findings.violation: WCAG-2.4.5 requires at least two independent mechanisms capable of leading a reader to this page, and this content page (not a step in a linear process) exposes exactly one, the primary navigation menu, with no site search, sitemap, or breadcrumb trail anywhere in the markup.

findings.evidence: is immediately followed by Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only. with no aria-describedby attribute on #promo referencing #s3-form-promo-error, and no other attribute on #promo associating it with that span.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to #promo so assistive technology announces the error text when the field receives focus.
findings.violation: WCAG-3.3.1 requires the nature of an identified error to be described to the reader in text as part of encountering the invalid item; the description text exists but carries no programmatic association to #promo, so a screen-reader user who tabs to the field hears only that it is invalid and has no reliable way to hear why.
